sections.h2: What is Morgantown, WV, and where does it sit?
sections.html:
Morgantown is the county seat of Monongalia County and lies along the Monongahela River, close to the Pennsylvania border. Wikipedia gives its 2020 census population as 30,347 and an estimate of 30,490 for 2024, which makes it the third-largest city in West Virginia. The wider metro area is estimated at about 140,000 people.

The city is small on the map, at 10.62 square miles, and it is about 75 miles south of Pittsburgh. Charleston is roughly 156 miles to the southwest.

Several neighborhoods began as separate towns and were annexed as Morgantown grew, and some are partly or fully outside the city limits even though everyone calls them Morgantown. The list includes:

  • First Ward, Second Ward and South Park near downtown
  • Sunnyside and Wiles Hill beside the downtown university campus
  • Evansdale, Greenmont and Woodburn
  • Suncrest, South Hills and North Hills
  • Sabraton, the Mileground and Easton, which are in part or entirely outside the city

That last point matters for sellers, because a house with a Morgantown address may sit outside the city limits.

sections.h2: How does West Virginia University shape the Morgantown housing market?
sections.html:
West Virginia University is the center of the local economy, and it shapes who buys and rents houses. WVU is the state's flagship public university. Wikipedia reports enrollment above 25,000 in 2024 and says the city hosts about 30,000 students, roughly the same as its permanent population.

Wikipedia describes Sunnyside, just north of downtown, as an older neighborhood that has long been known for student housing. A house in or near that area is often valued as a rental, not a family home, so the buyer pool leans toward investors.

The health system adds to the job base. According to WVU Government Relations, WVU Medicine supported 56,224 jobs statewide in fiscal year 2024. Another source, the Morgantown airport's economic baseline study, reported that WVU employed 6,500 people in 2011 and called it the largest single employer in the area. That figure is old, so treat it as a sense of scale.

If your house is a student rental with a lease running, tell any buyer the lease dates up front, since they affect when a buyer can take possession.

sections.h2: What does a Morgantown landlord need to know before selling?
sections.html:
Every rental unit inside the city is registered and inspected on a regular cycle. The city's rental information page says registered rentals are inspected once every three years under the International Property Maintenance Code, and owners must correct any violations found.

The city's code enforcement page explains the history. From 1979 until 1989 Morgantown followed housing codes written by city officials and approved by City Council. In 1989 the State of West Virginia adopted its first official written housing code.

TopicWhat the city says
Who must registerRental housing inside city limits
Inspection cycleOnce every 3 years
Code usedInternational Property Maintenance Code
DepartmentCode Enforcement, focused on safe buildings and rental units
Permits and licensingHandled through the Morgantown Access Portal

If you plan to sell a student rental, pull your registration and your last inspection result first. An open violation does not stop a sale, but it gives a conventional buyer a reason to negotiate. An investor paying cash can usually take on the repair list, so the price is the main question.

sections.h2: How do Morgantown's roads, transit and airport affect a sale?
sections.html:
Morgantown is served by I-79, I-68, US 19, US 119, WV 7 and WV 705. Buyers who commute pay attention to which of these a house is near.

Morgantown also has two systems you will not find elsewhere in the state. The Mountain Line Transit Authority runs most of the bus service, and its Grey Line operates every day of the year between Clarksburg and Pittsburgh International Airport. The Morgantown Personal Rapid Transit system has five stations and covers 8.65 miles. Its stations are Walnut, Beechurst, Engineering, Towers and Medical.

  • Morgantown Municipal Airport sits about 3 miles northeast of downtown on US 119.
  • North Central West Virginia Airport is about 35 miles away by road.
  • Pittsburgh International is about 80 miles away.

Describe your house's access to these routes accurately and let the buyer judge.

sections.h2: What is the climate like, and how does it affect a Morgantown house?
sections.html:
Morgantown has four distinct seasons at the boundary of humid subtropical and humid continental climates. The January daily mean is 32.0 degrees, and average annual snowfall is 27.6 inches. Summers are hot and humid, with a July mean of 74.1 degrees and about 13.2 days a year at or above 90.

Precipitation is generous. May through July is the wettest period, according to Wikipedia's summary of 1991 to 2020 airport normals. For a house, that means gutters, grading and basement moisture are routine inspection topics, and a recent roof or drainage repair helps a listing.

Whatever the house's age, a recent roof or drainage repair is worth mentioning to any buyer.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work for a Morgantown house?
sections.html:
The Monongalia County Assessor values the property and the County Sheriff's Tax Office collects the tax. The assessor's page for new residents states that real and personal property are assessed to the owner of record on July 1. If you sell after that date, the tax year still reflects you as owner, so plan for how the current bill will be handled at closing.

The Sheriff's Tax Office mails statements in July and sells delinquent real estate taxes in November, according to its website. State rules set the payment calendar:

  • Bills are issued on or after July 15.
  • The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1.
  • Paying before those dates earns a 2.5 percent discount.
  • Delinquent taxes accrue interest at 9 percent a year, per the West Virginia Tax Division.

For questions about paying real estate taxes, the assessor's website directs residents to the Sheriff's tax department at 304-291-7244. A tax lien that goes unpaid can complicate a sale, so confirm the status with the title company early.

sections.h2: What does selling a Morgantown house cost at closing?
sections.html:
The main government charge is the West Virginia transfer excise tax. Under section 11-22-2, the rate is $1.10 for each $500 of value, plus an additional county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 that a county commission may raise. The seller, as grantor, normally pays, and a $20 fee also goes to the state's Affordable Housing Fund.

At a base combined rate of $1.65 per $500, a $200,000 sale works out to $660. That is arithmetic from the statute, not a quote, and your county's current rate and the deed's stated value control. A will or an intestate list of heirs is excluded from the tax under section 11-22-1.

A traditional sale adds agent commissions, repairs requested after inspection and carrying costs while the house is listed. A cash sale to Cash Home Buyers is aimed at skipping those steps, and an offer depends on the property. If it does not work for you, you owe nothing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a rental house in Morgantown with open code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires owners to correct violations found at inspection, but an investor paying cash may buy the property as is. Check the registration and your latest inspection result first so the title company has the facts.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Monongalia County?
faqs.a: The Monongalia County Sheriff's Tax Office collects real estate and personal property taxes. The Assessor values the property. Statements are mailed in July, and delinquent real estate taxes are sold in November.

faqs.q: Is a house outside the Morgantown city limits treated differently?
faqs.a: Possibly. Areas such as the Mileground, Easton and parts of Sabraton are in part or entirely outside city limits, so ask the city and county offices which rules cover your address.

faqs.q: Do I owe transfer tax if I inherited my Morgantown house and sell it?
faqs.a: The tax applies to the deed when you sell. Transfers by will or through a list of heirs are excluded, so receiving the house from the estate is not taxed that way, but your sale deed to the buyer generally is.

faqs.q: How quickly can a cash sale close in Morgantown?
faqs.a: It depends on title work and recording, not on a lender. Ask for a target closing date in writing and confirm the title company that will handle the deed.
